finding: Pet names are two-part pools per creature family: 312 part rows over six families; one first half plus one second half, with the family name as fallback (ObjectMgr.cpp 8076-8147; pet_name_generation.sql).

Character-name gate runs in order: invalid characters, length, mixed scripts, three same letters, reserved names, profanity; the two-letter GM suffix rule is hard-coded in two places (ObjectMgr.cpp 9294-9313, 9005, 9108).

Faction map: 841 template rows, each with three group bitmasks and explicit lists of up to four enemies and four friends; runtime checks explicit lists before masks and treats same faction as friendly, plus a hates-all-except-friends flag (Unit.cpp 7017-7031; DBCStructure.h 990-1015).

Ambient speech: 18,591 lines over 4,175 creatures and 12,159 groups; 10,120 groups hold one line and 611 hold three. A pick is weighted-random among lines this creature has not said in that group, clearing when all are used (CreatureTextMgr.cpp 294-340).

Speech options: seven reusable option sets bound to 49 groups, giving trigger chance, cooldown (ms, rounded up to seconds) and player-only gate (CreatureTextMgr.cpp 284-287; Creature.cpp 3891-3897; update 2026_07_14_03.sql).
Gossip greetings: 8,361 npc_text rows with up to eight weighted variants; the server sends every weight and the client picks (QueryHandler.cpp 333). 7,368 rows use one slot, 989 use two or more.

Signs and tombstones: 165 text objects (type 9) point to a first page; 1,951 pages link by NextPage. Of 709 chain heads, 415 are single pages and 47 are three-page chains. The server returns the whole chain in one reply; 24 text objects point at missing pages (QueryHandler.cpp 361-410; ObjectMgr.cpp 6503).
Zone story in three lines: no zone-intro table has rows (areatable_dbc schema only). Closest analogues are the 47 three-page sign chains and the 611 three-line speech groups; the note says so.

Donor defects kept as ideas: unbounded NextPage walk (QueryHandler.cpp 391), dangling text-object pages (no loader check), hard-coded name rule. Fixes are in the sketch and section 3 of the note. Decision: adapt.

Pet names: same two-part rule; 260 pool rows in the base dump (line 4633) and in the archive copy, over five families (no family 26125). Only server code and this pool are read; world data is otherwise absent from the repo.

Faction reaction order is group enemy first, then explicit enemy, then group friend, then explicit friend, then reverse, then neutral; reputation overrides apply to player-controlled units (Relations.cpp 107-184). No same-faction shortcut in the struct check (DBCStructure.h 425). Faction table content is not in the repo.

Zone alarm: a guard or civilian entering combat with a player, or a guard dying to a player, broadcasts a zone-under-attack message with the zone id to every open-world player of the opposite team (CreatureAI.cpp 58-62; guard_ai.cpp 60; World.cpp 1860-1874). No cooldown in the path read; scope is whole team, not zone.
Guard barks: one of three aggro lines for one guard type, picked by a uniform roll with repeats possible (guard_ai.cpp 44-48). Other guard types not read.
Text objects use a 5.55556-yard interaction distance (GameObject.cpp 2444-2448). The page query loops on Next_Page with no cycle guard (QueryHandler.cpp 382, 412). Page text data is not in the repo.
Creature speech: script text dump of about 2,778 rows (scriptdev2.sql 705-726), keyed by id and used by C++ at the event; counts approximate; the dump has no per-group trigger or cooldown fields.

Donor defects kept as ideas: team-wide alarm with no rate limit, group-first faction order, no same-faction shortcut, unbounded page walk. Fixes are in the sketch and section 3 of the note. Decision: adapt (rate limit fixed in sketch).
